signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades under heavy pressure as JPY outperformance collides with a sharp WTI crude sell-off. JPY 1W average performance sits at +2.101% across 7 pairs while CAD lags at -0.833%, creating a massive 2.934% G10 spread. Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz initially buoyed energy, but news of progress on reopening the corridor has triggered a -5.61% collapse in WTI to $79.9, stripping away CAD's primary commodity support. Despite a 125bp carry advantage for CAD (BoC 2.25% vs BoJ 1.0%), the JPY safe-haven bid and positive ESI of +22.9 are dominating the cross. USD/JPY remains below its SMA20/50/200 cluster, confirming the broad JPY strength regime. Risk: Diplomatic talks fail and Hormuz tensions reignite, sparking a crude reversal that rescues CAD shorts.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options + Geopolitical Volatility
signals.text: USD/JPY is testing the 157.19 level, holding well below its SMA20 (162.34) and SMA50 (161.31) resistance. While the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%) structurally favors the USD, the options market is pricing in aggressive downside protection with a 25d RR at -3.19. This strong put skew suggests institutional hedging for a deeper JPY recovery despite the wide OIS carry gap. JPY COT LF net short remains extreme at -124,575, leaving the pair highly sensitive to short-covering if the Strait of Hormuz de-escalation continues. JPY's positive ESI of +22.9 further supports the fundamental case for JPY strength over the Fed's hold stance. Risk: Atlanta Fed's GDPNow 6.2% estimate translates into hard data, forcing a hawkish Fed repricing that overwhelms JPY momentum.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5872, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5795/0.5792/0.5826). RBNZ holds at 2.5%. The real policy rate for NZD is deeply accommodative at -1.56% compared to the Fed's restrictive +1.51%, yet the data outperformance suggests a looming squeeze on crowded spec shorts. Retail sentiment is also extreme with 90% short on NZD/CAD and 85% short on NZD/CHF, confirming broad retail fading of NZD strength. Risk: RBNZ unexpectedly pivots to 'Hold' at the September 2 meeting, validating the speculative short thesis and breaking the SMA200 support.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Volatility + Carry + Technical Levels
signals.text: USD/CHF at 0.8092 is exhibiting extreme volatility pricing, with an IV of 24.5% against an HV30 of 6.2%, creating a massive +18.3% Vol Risk Premium. The pair is currently trading below its SMA20 (0.8106) but holding above its SMA50 (0.8029). While the 375bp Fed-SNB carry differential (Fed 3.75% vs SNB 0.0%) is the largest in the G10 space, the options market is demanding a massive premium for protection, likely due to CHF's safe-haven role during Middle East headlines. COT LF net short of -11,635 on CHF shows specs are not yet positioned for a full haven flight, but the VRP suggests an imminent regime shift. Risk: VIX closes above 20, triggering a collapse in the carry trade and driving USD/CHF through the 0.8029 SMA50 support.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Carry vs Positioning Alignment
signals.text: GBP/USD is at 1.3434, comfortably positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster near 1.3400. The Fed-BoE carry spread is currently neutral (0bp), removing the usual USD advantage seen in other pairs. COT LF net long for GBP is robust at +36,661 (67.3% long), indicating institutional conviction in Sterling's resilience. However, the options market is slightly cautious with a 25d RR of -0.56, and the VRP of +4.8% suggests investors are paying up for downside hedges despite the bullish technical setup. This represents a mature trend where positioning is aligned with price but insurance demand is rising. Risk: A break below the 1.3365 SMA50 support triggers a liquidation of the +36k spec long contracts.
